topic_tag: a craft guild and a city's glass trade
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.

worlds.passage: In 1480 the glassmakers of a river city formed a guild with its own officers and rules. Its officers required every member to build a furnace that burned through the night instead of being banked at dusk. Tax rolls show the same forty workshops scattered across the city in 1480 and in 1530, but the duty they paid on finished glass, charged at an unchanged rate per piece, was twice as large in 1530, and by then glass cups turn up in the inventories of laborers' homes. According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.
worlds.explanation: With the same workshops and an unchanged rate per piece, twice the duty means twice the glass, so the guild "doubled" the trade. "Elevated" fails because glass became common enough for laborers' homes. "Confined" fails because the workshops stayed scattered across the city, and "abandoned" fails because the members kept paying duty on glass.

elevated.why: Glass becoming an everyday good suggests lower, not higher, standing.

confined.why: The trade was not restricted to one place.

abandoned.quote: the duty they paid on finished glass
abandoned.why: Members still producing taxed glass had not left the trade.

worlds.passage: In 1480 the glassmakers of a river city formed a guild with its own officers and rules. Its officers spent the guild's dues on gifts of glass to the city council and to visiting princes, and they won its masters the right to wear a councillor's furred robe. Tax rolls show the same forty workshops scattered across the city in 1480 and in 1530, paying about the same duty on finished glass at an unchanged rate per piece, and by 1530 a master's daughter could marry into the oldest merchant families. According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.
worlds.explanation: Gifts to princes, councillors' robes, and marriages into old families show the trade's standing rising, so the guild "elevated" it. "Doubled" fails because the duty, at an unchanged rate, stayed about the same. "Confined" fails because the workshops stayed scattered, and "abandoned" fails because the members kept producing taxed glass.

doubled.quote: about the same duty on finished glass
doubled.why: Unchanged duty at an unchanged rate means output did not grow.

confined.why: The trade was not restricted to one place.

abandoned.why: The members stayed in the trade.

worlds.passage: In 1480 the glassmakers of a river city formed a guild with its own officers and rules. After a workshop fire spread across three streets in 1491, its officers had the council forbid any furnace within the walls and grant the guild one small island downstream. Tax rolls list forty workshops on that island in 1530, paying about the same duty on finished glass as the forty in the city had paid in 1480, and glass was still the plain cup of the ordinary household. According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.
worlds.explanation: Furnaces were barred from the city and the workshops ended up on one island, so the guild "confined" the trade. "Doubled" fails because the duty stayed about the same. "Elevated" fails because glass remained a plain household cup, and "abandoned" fails because forty workshops kept working on the island.

doubled.quote: about the same duty on finished glass

elevated.quote: the plain cup of the ordinary household

abandoned.quote: Tax rolls list forty workshops on that island
abandoned.why: The members kept making glass, only in a new place.

worlds.passage: In 1480 the glassmakers of a river city formed a guild with its own officers and rules. By the 1500s the city's wool merchants were paying better returns than any furnace, and the guild's rules let a master keep his rank and his vote after selling his furnace. Tax rolls list forty guild workshops paying duty on finished glass in 1480 and none in 1530, when the city's cups and windowpanes came from unlicensed furnaces in every quarter, run by newcomers the guild had never admitted. According to one economic historian, within fifty years the guild had ______ the city's glass trade.
worlds.explanation: Masters could sell their furnaces without losing rank, and by 1530 no guild workshop paid duty while outsiders made the city's glass, so the guild "abandoned" the trade. "Doubled" and "elevated" fail because the guild no longer took part in a trade now run by unlicensed newcomers. "Confined" fails because those furnaces stood in every quarter.

doubled.why: A guild with no workshops left did not multiply the trade.

elevated.why: The trade passed to unlicensed newcomers, which did not raise its standing.

confined.why: The trade was spread across the city.
